claims.text: I01: The Universal Declaration grounds equal dignity and rights independently of distinctions named in Article 2. This is a normative framework, not a campaign-effect estimate. Source: [United Nations. 1948. Universal Declaration of Human Rights, arts. 1–2.](https://www.un.org/en/about-us/universal-declaration-of-human-rights)

claims.text: I02: Spain’s General Advertising Law Article 3(a) explicitly addresses advertising that attacks dignity; its consolidated text was checked on 2026-10-20, last update shown 2023-03-01. Application to a case requires jurisdictional and factual analysis. Source: [España. 1988. Ley 34/1988, General de Publicidad, art. 3(a).](https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-1988-26156#a3)

claims.text: I03: A visual discourse analysis of 15 Nordic fast-fashion advertisements identifies complex portrayals that need not dislodge stereotypes. This bounded sample is not an industry-wide prevalence measure. Source: [Srivastava, Sonali, Terhi-Anna Wilska, and Johanna Sjöberg. 2022. Girls’ portrayals in fast fashion advertisements. Consumption Markets & Culture 25(6):501–524.](https://doi.org/10.1080/10253866.2022.2067149)

Media International Australia 161(1):86–100.](https://doi.org/10.1177/1329878X16665177)

claims.text: I07: Pantano models online diffusion around a particular luxury campaign using negative stereotypes. The issue year is 2021, with online-first publication in 2020; the event does not provide a universal causal law. Source: [Pantano, Eleonora. 2021. When a luxury brand bursts: Modelling the social media viral effects of negative stereotypes adoption leading to brand hate. Journal of Business Research 123:117–125.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jbusres.2020.09.049)

claims.text: I08: The supplied 2026 practice bank case GD16 connects textile production location, fair working conditions, materials and communication. I09: Freire’s problem-posing relation treats teacher and learners as investigators of a shared object. Our fashion tasks are a pedagogical adaptation, not an intervention validated by that text. Source: Freire, Paulo. 2000. Pedagogy of the Oppressed. 30th anniversary edition. Continuum. ISBN 9781501305313. Supplied vault edition verified on title and copyright pages.
